What is answer engine optimization?

Answer engine optimization is the practice of making a web page easy for ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and Perplexity to crawl, understand, and cite. It covers robots access, structured data, identity, and short answers that sit directly under question headings so a model can quote you without guessing. Teams use it when search traffic still arrives but brand mentions in AI answers do not.

How do you make a page easy to cite?

Start with a single H1, question-style H2s, and a 40 to 60 word answer in the first paragraph. Add FAQPage and Organization JSON-LD, allow GPTBot in robots.txt, and publish llms.txt with links to your docs. Cite sources such as NIST and Wikipedia when you quote a figure. Keep at least 300 words in the HTML itself.

Which signals matter most?

  • Crawler access in robots.txt
  • JSON-LD that names the organization
  • Visible dates and a byline

FAQPage Lets models extract Q and A pairs

Across 1,800 audited sites the median GEO score sits near 59 out of 100, and 76 percent ship JSON-LD. Pages under 300 words rarely get cited. Use schema.org types, keep copy in the server HTML, and link to an about page so the entity is unambiguous. That combination is what this fixture is built to demonstrate for the checker tests.

Extra copy keeps the word count above three hundred words so the content check can pass. Answer engines still prefer specific numbers, named authors, and outbound citations over slogans. If the HTML is an empty shell, none of the other work counts. Northline publishes this page as a complete example of the on-page bar, including lists, a table, dates, and a contact path.
